claims.text: The trip record and the driver's own trace describe one completed metered RYDE_X ride from Woodlands MRT (Exit C) to Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 2. Under POL-RD-01 the governing length is the trace polyline, and EV-GPS-00302 records trace_distance_km of 28.2 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km on EV-TRIP-00302. The excess is 6.2 km, which is 28.18% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass — 28.18% is greater than 20% and 6.2 km is greater than 0.8 km — so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

The driver cannot attack the measurement through the trace. EV-GPS-00302 is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 235 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. There is no broken stretch, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval above 30 seconds, so the 28.2 km figure stands and the excess cannot be written off as a data artefact.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider has discharged the initial burden: the trip identifier TRP-00302 matches across EV-TRIP-00302, EV-GPS-00302 and EV-FARE-00302, and an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold is measured on an unimpaired trace. The burden has therefore shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The counterparty_statement offers only 'SLE was heavy at the CTE merge so I stayed on CTE all the way down' — a general traffic assertion with no artifact named, which under POL-RD-08 discharges nothing.

The traffic excuse fails on the bundle as well as on its own silence. The only advisory artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00302-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers the SLE or the CTE in this window. Under POL-RD-13 that is fatal to the driver's excuse: the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight. The deviation stands at the measured 6.2 km against the booked 22.0 km optimal.

There is no rider-requested detour to exclude. EV-CHAT-00302 is a completed export with message_count 0 and an empty message array, and EV-TRIP-00302 carries chat_message_count 0. With no rider instruction in the chat log, POL-RD-04(a) to (c) cannot be met, no distance is excluded, and POL-RD-14 has nothing to consider. The driver cannot say the rider asked for the CTE.

Nor was the destination moved. On EV-TRIP-00302 the pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at fields are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 cannot re-quote the optimal route and the booked 22.0 km baseline stands. The vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply either.

The fare model is METERED on EV-FARE-00302 and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not displace POL-RD-02 and the distance-and-time recomputation runs. The driver's second point — 'Surge was on, that is why it is more' — is no answer: the surge multiplier of 1.2 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00302, the only artifact that carries it, and POL-RD-02 applies that same multiplier to the recomputed optimal fare, so surge inflates both sides of the subtraction and explains none of the 12.27 gap.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic is as follows. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 28.0 optimal min) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 ERP on the optimal route = (28.14 x 1.2) + 0.80 + 1.50 = 33.768 + 2.30 = 36.068. charged_total on EV-FARE-00302 is 48.34. Refund = 48.34 - 36.068 = 12.272, rounded up to SGD 12.30. That is far above the 0.50 de minimis and only 25.4% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 12.30.

The rider's 'extra ERP' request is satisfied inside that figure, not beside it. Three gantries were charged totalling 4.50: BKE (Woodlands towards PIE) at 1.50, flagged on_optimal_route true, plus CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at 2.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at 1.00, both flagged on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route ERP of 3.00 is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare counts only on-optimal-route gantry charges. Itemising it is correct; adding 3.00 on top of the 12.30 would be the double count POL-RD-09(1) forbids.

Both off-route crossings are real and were actually made, so this is not a phantom-line matter under POL-RD-09(4). The driver's nearest fix to the CTE Braddell gantry is 0.0 m away at 08:14:45 and the nearest fix to the CTE Moulmein gantry is 0.0 m away at 08:20:55, per the erp_gantry_proximity block of EV-GPS-00302. These are charges for gantries the vehicle genuinely passed on a corridor the optimal route does not use, and they are refunded through the recomputation rather than as a standalone correction.

POL-RD-08's extra corroboration requirement is not engaged here. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d on EV-RPROF-00302 is 0, well below the trigger of 4 claims, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so this claim does not need corroboration beyond the gps_trace. The rider's profile adds no obstacle and, under POL-GEN-01, none of its other fields may be used against the claim.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires on this record. Every artifact that carries a deciding fact — EV-TRIP-00302, EV-GPS-00302 and EV-FARE-00302 — is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, so under POL-GEN-02 the confidence cap does not drop below the 0.70 floor; the trip identifiers all match; pickup and dropoff timestamps on the admitted artifacts do not conflict by more than 10 minutes; the trace is not impaired; and no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact. The only sub-1.0 artifact is the MISSING advisory, which is cited for its absence and carries no fact. The dispute is therefore capable of a monetary ruling and the rider's 12.30 refund should issue.

One point is worth stating plainly rather than overreaching. The excess of 28.18% clears the 20% establishment line but falls below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality line, so POL-RD-06's driver-profile uplift is not triggered on this trip and FULL_REFUND is not available on these facts. The honest measure of the rider's loss is the POL-RD-02 recomputation of 12.30, and against a contested amount of 15.00 that is the bulk of what the rider actually asked for.

claims.text: The deviation on this trip is established but is NOT material, and that distinction governs the driver's exposure. The trace shows an excess of 6.2 km, 28.18% of the 22.0 km optimal route: it clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate of 0.8 km and 20%, but it is far below either materiality threshold of 8.0 km or 50%. Because the excess is not material, the POL-RD-06 driver_profile consequences - a FULL_REFUND uplift in place of the POL-RD-02 partial, and a driver-conduct referral - simply do not arise, and the POL-RD-02 partial is the ceiling on any refund.

The driver's profile supports no adverse finding. His deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the 3 that the POL-RD-06 test requires, and 1 flag against 70 completed_trips_90d is a ratio of 0.014, far under the alternative 0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no remedy uplift and no conduct referral can attach. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day counter the clause names, which POL-GEN-01 forbids.

The rider's benchmark of 'usually around $32' attributes the whole gap to the detour when a large part of it is platform surge. The fare_breakdown records a surge_multiplier of 1.2 and a surge_amount of 7.17 on this trip, applied to the base, distance and time charges. The rider's comparison cannot be read as though the alleged detour caused the entire 48.34 - 32.00 difference, and the only refund POL-RD-02 supports is the arithmetic one, computed with that same 1.2 multiplier read off the fare_breakdown.

The refund the rider can actually recover is capped by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic at SGD 12.30, not the SGD 15.00 claimed. charged_total is 48.34. The optimal-route recomputation is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.0 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 of on-optimal-route ERP = 36.068. The difference is 12.272, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving 12.30 on a 48.34 charge - a refund share of 25.4%, nowhere near the 90% of charged_total that would trigger FULL_REFUND.

The rider asks separately for 'the extra ERP back'. Under POL-RD-09(1) there is no separate ERP refund to award on top of the distance refund: the off-route gantries (CTE Braddell Rd at 2.00 and CTE Moulmein Rd at 1.00, 3.00 together) are already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which charges only the single gantry lying on the optimal route (BKE, 1.50). Those lines may be itemised for transparency, but adding them to the POL-RD-02 figure would be the exact double-count the clause forbids.

There is no billing-integrity correction to make under POL-RD-09(4). Each of the three charged gantries is matched to the driver's own trace, with the nearest fix sitting 0.0 m from each gantry's coordinates, so no line is charged for a gantry the vehicle never crossed, and the airport surcharge line is 0.00 on a Woodlands-to-Marina-Bay trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. Nothing on the ledger supports a standalone refund beyond the POL-RD-02 figure.

The rider's characterisation that the driver 'went all the way round via the CTE' overstates the record. The first charged gantry, BKE (Woodlands towards PIE), is flagged on_optimal_route true and is matched to the trace at a 0.0 m fix distance, so the driver began on the optimal corridor. The deviation is confined to the tail past the Moulmein exit, which is precisely why the measured excess is a modest 6.2 km and not a material one.

The driver's recorded explanation - that the SLE was heavy at the CTE merge, so he stayed on the CTE - is an asserted external traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 requires it to be tested against this trip's traffic_advisory and nothing else. The only such artifact, EV-ADVIS-00302-01, is MISSING: its status is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING) fired, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the excess stands at the 6.2 km the trace measures. I disclose that impairment. What the gap does not do is aggravate the finding: under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact can carry no fact against either party, so the driver's untestable explanation cannot be read as a deliberate detour or used to support any conduct finding.

To the rider and the driver: this is a provisional ruling. Both advocates' arithmetic is correct, and I adopt it.

THE DEVIATION. On this trip's own evidence the route deviation is established. EV-GPS-00302 (the driver's trace) records 28.2 km against the booked optimal of 22.0 km on EV-TRIP-00302 — an excess of 6.2 km, or 28.18%. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 235 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, so the 28.2 km measurement stands. The excess does not, however, reach materiality (8.0 km or 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the 3 the clause requires and below the 0.05 ratio over at least 40 trips (1/70). No remedy uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise. I note the driver claim that mentions prior_deviation_flags: that lifetime counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not used for any finding.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE. The driver says the SLE was heavy at the CTE merge. That is an asserted external traffic cause and is tested against this trip's traffic advisory only. The sole such artifact, EV-ADVIS-00302-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). Under POL-RD-13 the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the excuse carries no weight; the deviation stands at the measured 6.2 km. The driver's assertion cites no advisory identifier, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and this is not an escalation. Equally, the missing artifact carries no fact against the driver.

THE FARE. The fare model on EV-FARE-00302 is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.0 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 on-optimal-route ERP = 36.068. Charged total = 48.34. Refund = 48.34 - 36.068 = 12.272, rounded up to SGD 12.30. The surge multiplier of 1.2 was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00302 and inflates both sides of the subtraction; it does not explain the gap. The refund is above the 0.50 de-minimis and only 25.4% of the charge, well short of the 90% that would make it a full refund.

THE ERP. Three gantries were billed, 4.50 in total: BKE 1.50 (on the optimal route) and two CTE gantries at 2.00 and 1.00 (off it). Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route 3.00 is already comprehended in the 12.30 recomputation, which counts only the on-route gantry. It is itemised for transparency but is not added on top. Both CTE crossings are genuine (nearest fixes 0.0 m), so there is no billing-integrity correction and no referral under POL-RD-09(4).

No rider-requested detour (EV-CHAT-00302 is empty), no pickup or dropoff amendment, and no pooled itinerary bear on the result.

OUTCOME. The rider is refunded SGD 12.30 of the 15.00 contested. Because that exceeds the automatic execution threshold of SGD 8.00, the amount is issued but held for release by a human reviewer rather than executed automatically. ledger.claim: The trip record and the driver's own trace describe one completed metered RYDE_X ride from Woodlands MRT (Exit C) to Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 2. The driver cannot attack the measurement through the trace. The counterparty_statement offers only 'SLE was heavy at the CTE merge so I stayed on CTE all the way down' — a general traffic assertion with no artifact named, which under POL-RD-08 discharges nothing.

The traffic excuse fails on the bundle as well as on its own silence. There is no rider-requested detour to exclude. EV-CHAT-00302 is a completed export with message_count 0 and an empty message array, and EV-TRIP-00302 carries chat_message_count 0. With no rider instruction in the chat log, POL-RD-04(a) to (c) cannot be met, no distance is excluded, and POL-RD-14 has nothing to consider. The driver cannot say the rider asked for the CTE.

Nor was the destination moved. On EV-TRIP-00302 the pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at fields are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 cannot re-quote the optimal route and the booked 22.0 km baseline stands. ledger.claim: The rider's benchmark of 'usually around $32' attributes the whole gap to the detour when a large part of it is platform surge. The fare_breakdown records a surge_multiplier of 1.2 and a surge_amount of 7.17 on this trip, applied to the base, distance and time charges. The rider's comparison cannot be read as though the alleged detour caused the entire 48.34 - 32.00 difference, and the only refund POL-RD-02 supports is the arithmetic one, computed with that same 1.2 multiplier read off the fare_breakdown.

The refund the rider can actually recover is capped by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic at SGD 12.30, not the SGD 15.00 claimed. charged_total is 48.34. The optimal-route recomputation is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.0 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 of on-optimal-route ERP = 36.068. The difference is 12.272, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving 12.30 on a 48.34 charge - a refund share of 25.4%, nowhere near the 90% of charged_total that would trigger FULL_REFUND.

The rider asks separately for 'the extra ERP back'. Under POL-RD-09(1) there is no separate ERP refund to award on top of the distance refund: the off-route gantries (CTE Braddell Rd at 2.00 and CTE Moulmein Rd at 1.00, 3.00 together) are already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which charges only the single gantry lying on the optimal route (BKE, 1.50). Those lines may be itemised for transparency, but adding them to the POL-RD-02 figure would be the exact double-count the clause forbids.

There is no billing-integrity correction to make under POL-RD-09(4). Each of the three charged gantries is matched to the driver's own trace, with the nearest fix sitting 0.0 m from each gantry's coordinates, so no line is charged for a gantry the vehicle never crossed, and the airport surcharge line is 0.00 on a Woodlands-to-Marina-Bay trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. Nothing on the ledger supports a standalone refund beyond the POL-RD-02 figure.

The rider's characterisation that the driver 'went all the way round via the CTE' overstates the record. The first charged gantry, BKE (Woodlands towards PIE), is flagged on_optimal_route true and is matched to the trace at a 0.0 m fix distance, so the driver began on the optimal corridor. The deviation is confined to the tail past the Moulmein exit, which is precisely why the measured excess is a modest 6.2 km and not a material one.

The driver's recorded explanation - that the SLE was heavy at the CTE merge, so he stayed on the CTE - is an asserted external traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 requires it to be tested against this trip's traffic_advisory and nothing else. The only such artifact, EV-ADVIS-00302-01, is MISSING: its status is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING) fired, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the excess stands at the 6.2 km the trace measures. I disclose that impairment. What the gap does not do is aggravate the finding: under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact can carry no fact against either party, so the driver's untestable explanation cannot be read as a deliberate detour or used to support any conduct finding.
